study.question: Does fav alone supply a practically sufficient transported orientation bit at the fixed-angle joint model, and does replacing the full-task bit by fav-only preserve the external-sign response?
study.hypothesis: Observed: full-task negative bridge AUC0.6689610675617089; omitting fav from ONLY the bit gives0.6683238588338976 (delta -0.0006372087), versus omitting cart0.6687360168102108 and buy0.6686467206742304. These are adaptive single-seed observations, not task rankings. Hypothesis: fav may carry the bit information underlying the negative-sign benefit, while cart/buy may be redundant or complementary. Necessary contribution does not imply sufficiency. Replace only bit source with fav-only and cross external sign to discriminate sufficiency from complementarity and arbitrary sign calibration.

study.proposed_difference: A new helper replaces cart/buy cotangents by shape/dtype-matched zeros ONLY for recomputing fav-only centered O, paired replacement, tangent Q and first-max-absolute pivot sign (zero ->+1). It uses the inherited exact reduction order (0+fav)+0. Attach that sign to the full-task canonical fixed-angle transfer; use both external signs. Full-task cells select their inherited expressions exactly. All helper computations execute in every variant. Only the custom context VJP selection changes, not the reported joint loss, capacity or forward architecture.
predictions: Predeclare practical sufficiency margin0.0001 absolute click AUC; this is an engineering threshold, not a significance level or equivalence confidence bound. Fav-only negative should fall no more than0.0001 below full-task negative if fav is practically sufficient for this bit in the current seed.

Fav-only should retain negative-minus-positive AUC gap direction if it carries the same signed response. Report the factorial interaction [fav-negative minus fav-positive] minus [all-negative minus all-positive] without assuming zero interaction.
At fixed state, bit-source replacement preserves transfer line/radius/support and changes at most its global sign. All-task replay predictions and metrics should reproduce existing signed controls.

Expected inference architecture and parameter count are identical; extra context-sized backward work raises or preserves training cost. Measure the increase; no equal-compute superiority claim from matched data passes alone.
falsifiers: Fav-only negative AUC more than0.0001 below the matched full-task negative rejects practical single-seed sufficiency.

Full-task/fav-only bit disagreement accompanied by a collapsed or reversed signed AUC gap contradicts the simple same-bit-information explanation; agreement and parity at fixed state without any new trajectory difference would instead limit discrimination.
Forward/state/private-gradient differences, geometry/support mismatches, nonfinite gradients or bridge failure invalidate the intended contrast.
A favorable one-seed AUC after many adaptive comparisons does not establish generalization, informative labels or causal mechanism; permitted paired repeats or stronger replacements may refute it.
alternative_explanations: The fav omission result reflects complementarity of all tasks, not fav-only sufficiency. Earlier raw fav-only context transfer g3-r0031-fav_context_only AUC0.6677933678779057 also failed to improve click-only0.6678548720585206; that different transfer mechanism cannot be promoted to evidence about the new bit.

Generic optimization perturbation, coordinate carrier, pivot sign imbalance or earlier trajectory changes could explain improvements. Historical bit removal negatives0.6687531802698141 and positives0.6687682991939847, click-bit substitution0.6687444859805948 and batch-roll label control0.6674639465810746 retain negative and null evidence but do not isolate every remaining path at the current model.

Full-task radius and gates still contain all auxiliary information, even in fav-only bit cells. This design cannot show complete removal of auxiliary signal, true-label informativeness or semantic gradient alignment.

Validation overfitting and seed-specific optimization remain plausible. Same-seed repeats are replay controls; no significance from independent-impression assumptions. Auxiliary labels match user/category/brand over24h and are not advertisement conversion attribution. Offline delayed-feedback visibility and publisher vocab/static assumptions limit deployment conclusions.
